description: Figure 18 is a composite of four grouped bar charts arranged in two panels, (a) and (b), each split into an upper and a lower sub-chart with its own y-axis labelled "DRX fraction"; all share the x-axis "True strain" with three conditions, 0.4, 0.5 and 0.9. The legend marks "Experiment" in tan and "3D CA" in green; small error bars appear only on the Experiment bars. (a) upper is labelled "Increasing ε̇ at 0.4 strain" and (a) lower "Decreasing ε̇ at 0.4 strain"; (b) upper is labelled "Decreasing T at 0.4 strain" and (b) lower "Increasing T at 0.4 strain". Printed values (Experiment/3D CA): increasing strain rate 0.757/0.769, 0.846/0.859, 0.958/0.979; decreasing strain rate 0.395/0.429, 0.955/0.991, 0.975/0.998; decreasing temperature 0.914/0.943, 0.963/0.954, 0.98/0.986; increasing temperature 0.757/0.769, 0.979/0.995, 0.99/0.998. In every condition the DRX fraction rises with true strain, the largest jump occurring between 0.4 and 0.5 strain, and the 3D CA bars track the experimental ones closely. The figure demonstrates that a transient change of strain rate or temperature imposed at 0.4 strain still drives DRX fraction toward ~1 by 0.9 strain, and that the CA model reproduces this evolution.

observations.observation: Figure 18 contains two panels, (a) and (b), each composed of an upper and a lower grouped bar chart sharing the x-axis 'True strain' with categories 0.4, 0.5 and 0.9, and y-axes labelled 'DRX fraction'.
The legend identifies two series: 'Experiment' (tan bars, drawn with small error bars) and '3D CA' (green bars).
Panel (a) upper, labelled 'Increasing ε̇ at 0.4 strain', prints Experiment 0.757, 0.846, 0.958 and 3D CA 0.769, 0.859, 0.979 at true strains 0.4, 0.5 and 0.9 respectively.
Panel (a) lower, labelled 'Decreasing ε̇ at 0.4 strain', prints Experiment 0.395, 0.955, 0.975 and 3D CA 0.429, 0.991, 0.998 at true strains 0.4, 0.5 and 0.9.
Panel (b) upper, labelled 'Decreasing T at 0.4 strain', prints Experiment 0.914, 0.963, 0.98 and 3D CA 0.943, 0.954, 0.986 at true strains 0.4, 0.5 and 0.9.
Panel (b) lower, labelled 'Increasing T at 0.4 strain', prints Experiment 0.757, 0.979, 0.99 and 3D CA 0.769, 0.995, 0.998 at true strains 0.4, 0.5 and 0.9.
The 0.4-strain value pair 0.757 (Experiment) / 0.769 (3D CA) appears both in panel (a) upper and in panel (b) lower, i.e. it is the common pre-transient reference state at true strain 0.4.
In each of the four sub-charts the DRX fraction increases monotonically with true strain, and the largest increase between consecutive strain levels occurs between 0.4 and 0.5 strain.

Across the four sub-charts the 3D CA value is equal to or slightly above the paired Experiment value at nearly every strain level, except in (b) upper at 0.5 strain where Experiment (0.963) exceeds 3D CA (0.954).
The lower sub-chart of panel (a) uses a broken/segmented y-scale: visible tick labels are 0.3, 0.4, 0.7 and 1.1, so the 0.4-strain bar at 0.395/0.429 sits far below the 0.5- and 0.9-strain bars.

The caption states the figure shows experimental and simulated evolutions of DRX fraction after varying deformation conditions at 0.4 strain, with (a) for varying strain rate and (b) for varying temperature.

The citing text states that after transiently increasing the strain rate at 0.4 strain the experimental DRX fraction increased from 75.7 % at 0.4 strain to 84.6 % at 0.5 strain, which corresponds to the 0.757 and 0.846 values printed in panel (a) upper.

The citing text states that after increasing the temperature the experimental DRX fraction increased from 75.7 % at 0.4 strain to 97.9 % at 0.5 strain, matching the 0.757 and 0.979 values printed in panel (b) lower.

The citing text states that for decreasing temperature the experimental recrystallization fraction increased slowly and the simulated DRX fraction increased more weakly than the experimental one, which agrees with the small Experiment-vs-3D CA gap in panel (b) upper.
